evidence.verdict: I checked the tagged sentences in Sections 0, Bottom line, 2, 3.1-3.3, 5 (the Reading of the matrix and the Basis lines) and 6 against their evidence.csv rows, and against the saved sources where a quote was in doubt. Most sentences hold up: the numbers, dates, quotes and most attributions match their rows (Intel probing, SK hynix warpage and IR, the X-ray dose figures and their arithmetic, the awards figures, and the 44-document method count, which I re-ran). Three sentences are wrong or unsupported and must be fixed. (1) Section 6 says ASE's sites and Micron's IR sites could not be read, but the evidence file uses rows fetched from aseglobal.com and micron.gcs-web.com, and run_log shows intc.com accepted scripts. (2) Section 0 item 4 says TSMC names no SoIC test method other than daisy chains, but its own input SYN-039 and ADDL-025 cite the SWTest deck's CPS probing for known-good SoIC stacks. (3) Section 3.3 says Samsung-led authors "replaced" the SAM scan, but the paper says it "developed an alternative". The should_fix items are attribution and tagging: vendor-led or university-led papers credited to the chipmaker (SYN-018, the ASE rows, the Samsung leakage paper); a PILOT cell for Samsung electrical test that its own Basis line says is lab; an Intel VM basis line stronger than SMP-033's note; a claim with no tag and claims with no evidence row; [I] attached to [F] ids; and NOT RETRIEVED / NOT DISCLOSED written in a form the rules do not allow. The minor items are wrong or missing ids.

compliance.verdict:
The dossier covers all five asks in substance, but it is not ready to hand over. There are 13 must_fix items:
- One ask is partly missing: ask 3 has no separate HBM4 and HBM4E answer.
- Four internal contradictions:
  - The bottom line says "two items" come close to production, but Section 5 rates four HBM or bonding cells PILOT.
  - The bottom line says sampling increases are "all development or proposals", but Section 3.1 has SK hynix's all-chip warpage method, which SK hynix says is "currently in use" [C].
  - Premise item 4 says TSMC names no SoIC method beyond daisy chains, but Section 3.2 cites TSMC's CPS test of the SoIC stack (ADDL-025).
  - Review-packet inference 4 says VM is not presented as cutting physical measurement. Section 3.3 and SMP-042 say Micron's wording may mean fewer measurements, and Samsung measures about 4% and fills the rest by ML.
- A wrong count in the bottom line: "X-ray CT named in 7" counts XRD, XRR and EDX papers; the real figure is 3. Optical is also overcounted (7 should be 6).
- Rule breaches:
  - claims with no tag, and claims admitted to have no evidence row;
  - missing data written in forms other than the two allowed ones, including 22 blank tool-vendor cells, "NOT NAMED" and "none named";
  - gaps.md lines outside the two forms, a truncated line, and two items logged as both NOT RETRIEVED and NOT DISCLOSED;
  - [C]/[F] double tags on 16 Section 1 rows;
  - verdict words outside [I];
  - award-table rows with no tag, and no SK hynix row.

review_packet.md meets its format: 15 claims, 5 inferences, 3 questions, about 1,000 words. Its content still needs fixing: inference 4, the inputs for inference 2, the PAPM-222 wording, an unsourced tool name, and missing confidence levels. gaps.md has 86 NOT RETRIEVED and 70 NOT DISCLOSED lines, matching its headers.
